## Summary

Adds a ↻ trailing action button in the Cookie Source picker row for OpenCode Go and OpenCode providers in the settings pane.

## Behaviour

1. Clears the cached browser cookie from Keychain
2. Re-imports from all supported browsers (using the provider's browser import order)
3. Stores the fresh cookie
4. Triggers an immediate provider refresh

If re-import fails (e.g. running outside the signed app bundle), the cache is still cleared and the next auto-refresh will complete the import.

## Evidence

The same code path (`CookieHeaderCache.clear` → `importSession` → `store`) is exercised by the CLI command. See `docs/proof/cli-cookie-refresh-proof.md` in PR #2262 for the full test matrix.

Button UI verified via signed-app screenshot: located in the Cookie Source picker trailing area alongside the cached timestamp and source dropdown.

## Related

- Issue: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2260
- CLI PR: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2262

target.title: feat: add codexbar cookie refresh CLI command
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `codexbar cookie refresh --provider <name>` CLI command to force re-import of browser cookies for cookie-authenticated providers.

**Note:** Settings-pane refresh buttons (↻) split into a separate PR: **#2264**.

## Behaviour

- `codexbar cookie refresh --provider opencodego` — clears Keychain cache, re-imports from all supported browsers, stores fresh cookie
- `codexbar cookie refresh --all` — refreshes OpenCode and OpenCode Go
- Falls back gracefully when `importSession` fails (code-signing entitlements required)
- Supports `--format text|json`, `--json`, `--json-only`, `--pretty`
- Uses the provider's automatic browser import order (scans all installed browsers via `preferredBrowsers: []`)

## Verified Behaviour

### Evidence

See `docs/proof/cli-cookie-refresh-proof.md` for full test matrix.

Key results:

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `cookie refresh --provider opencodego` | ✅ JSON output: `"status": "cleared"` |
| Before: Keychain `cookie.opencodego` | `storedAt: 2026-07-17T18:25:50Z` |
| After: Keychain lookup | ❌ Not found (cache cleared) |
| After CodexBar.app refresh | ✅ Cookie re-imported with fresh `storedAt` |
| `--provider nonexistent` | ✅ `"Unknown provider: nonexistent"` |
| `--all` | ✅ Targets only OpenCode + OpenCodeGo |
| `--format json --pretty` | ✅ Valid JSON output |
| Build | ✅ `swift build` zero errors |

### End-to-end flow

```
CLI command                         CodexBar.app (menu bar)
┌──────────────────────┐            ┌─────────────────────┐
│ cookie refresh       │            │ auto-refresh detects │
│ --provider opencodego│            │ missing cache        │
│                      │            │                      │
│ ① Clear Keychain ✅  │  ──────→  │ ② SweetCookieKit     │
│ ② Import browser ❌  │  (fail)   │    import from Chrome │
│    (unsigned binary) │            │ ③ Store in Keychain  │
│ ③ Print "cleared"    │            │ ④ Refresh usage ✅   │
└──────────────────────┘            └─────────────────────┘
```

### Known Limitation

`OpenCodeCookieImporter.importSession()` requires code-signing entitlements unavailable in debug CLI builds. The command clears the cache and falls back — the actual re-import happens when CodexBar.app (with proper entitlements) refreshes. Same behaviour as `codexbar cache clear --cookies` which also clears without importing.

## Related

- Issue: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2260
- Settings PR: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2264

target.title: Doubao: query Coding/Agent Plan usage via arkcli CLI
target.body:
## Summary

- Replace the Volcengine AK/SK signed API with `arkcli usage plan` CLI (SSO-based) for fetching Coding Plan and Agent Plan usage
- Split Doubao menu card into "Coding Plan" and "Agent Plan" sections with group headers
- Replace placeholder smiley icon with official Volcengine logo SVG

## Why

The signed Volcengine API (`GetCodingPlanUsage` / `GetAgentPlanUsage`) required users to obtain AK/SK credentials separately and did not work well. The `arkcli` CLI uses the same SSO session the user already has, making setup trivial - just install arkcli and `arkcli auth login`.

## Changes

- `DoubaoUsageFetcher`: new `fetchCodingPlanUsage(runArkcli:)` runs `arkcli usage plan` and decodes the JSON response. Old Volcengine signer code removed.
- `DoubaoAPIFetchStrategy`: try arkcli CLI first, fall back to Ark API key rate-limit probe.
- `MenuCardView`: split Doubao metrics into two groups (Coding Plan / Agent Plan) with section headers. Other providers unaffected (`guard provider == .doubao`).
- `ProviderIcon-doubao.svg`: official Volcengine logo (MIT-licensed, from thesvg.org).
- Tests updated to match new arkcli JSON format and strategy interface.

Closes #1724.

target.title: Show DeepSeek Platform usage with cost summary
target.body:
## Summary

- move DeepSeek Platform cost and token history from **Show credits & extra usage** to **Cost summary**
- show DeepSeek details inline for Inline, Submenu, and Both because DeepSeek has no cost submenu
- keep balance and browser sign-in guidance independent, while limiting detailed usage to the active token account

## Why

DeepSeek detailed Platform data is cost and token usage, but its fetch and rendering were gated by the unrelated credits/extras setting. Users could therefore authenticate successfully and see their balance while the available usage chart remained hidden.

This is a follow-up to #2135.

## Consent boundary

DeepSeek detailed usage continues to use the existing selected Chrome session. Enabling any non-Off **Cost summary** option is intentionally treated as consent to run that Platform usage probe and show its cost and token data inline. **Show credits & extra usage** no longer controls this probe. Turning Cost summary off disables detailed usage, while balance and sign-in guidance remain independent.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter MenuCardDeepSeekTests` (8 tests)
- `swift test --filter ProviderSettingsDescriptorTests` (36 tests)
- `make check`
- packaged DeepSeek CLI live probe with the signed-in Chrome profile
- manually checked a fresh build with DeepSeek Cost summary enabled and disabled

The full sharded test runner previously reached 46 green groups before its final mixed process/spend group hit the watchdog; the affected spend-controller suite passed separately (24 tests).

target.title: Preserve Claude snapshots across CLI parse failures
target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve the existing Claude snapshot when repeated terminal CLI usage parse failures reach the failure gate, so the card can surface the failure without falling back to `Not fetched yet`.
- Gate parse-failure preservation on the terminal fetch attempt kind, so Web/OAuth parse failures still clear stale prior data once the failure gate surfaces the error.
- Keep a prior Max/Pro/Team/Ultra subscription snapshot visible when a later CLI probe returns a subscription-only response without quota data; Education/no-prior paths still use `Limits not available`.
- Add regression coverage for repeated CLI parse failures, subscription-only responses with prior subscription limits, and Web parse failures clearing stale snapshots.

Refs #2241.

## Tests
- `make check`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `swiftc -parse Sources/CodexBar/UsageStore+Refresh.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeResilienceTests.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeEducationAvailabilityTests.swift`
- `swiftc -parse Tests/CodexBarTests/ClaudeWebRefreshResilienceTests.swift`

Attempted but not completed locally:
- `swift test --filter ClaudeResilienceTests`
- `swift test --filter ClaudeEducationAvailabilityTests`
- `swift test --skip-update --filter ClaudeResilienceTests`
- `swift test --skip-update --filter ClaudeWebRefreshResilienceTests`

Those SwiftPM runs stalled while resolving/downloading the Sparkle 2.9.3 binary artifact before tests executed. A direct `curl -L --max-time 60` download of the same artifact completed successfully earlier, so this looks like a local SwiftPM artifact resolver stall rather than a source-level test failure.

I did not run live Claude provider probes because the repository guidance says live provider probes, browser-cookie imports, and real account paths should not be run unless explicitly requested. The behavior here is covered with stubbed provider strategies and the hosted CI test shards.

## Compatibility Risk
Low. The change only affects Claude refresh failure publication when a prior Claude snapshot already exists, and the follow-up gate keeps stale Web/OAuth parse failures from being preserved as CLI data.

target.title: Document universal quota planning design
target.body:
## Summary

- define a universal, descriptor-driven quota-planning capability
- lead with learned full-session capacity (`N`), with theoretical capacity before reset (`M`) and an asymmetric reachability verdict
- isolate calibration by provider, account, pair, and fetch strategy while composing with pace per long metric
- specify the Codex, Claude, and Antigravity rollout, fail-closed behavior, lifecycle, presentation, and test boundaries

## Product decision

`N` is the headline because it answers how many full short-window allowance equivalents the remaining weekly quota can fund at the recently observed workload mix. `M` is the every-window-flat-out upper bound before reset and deliberately ignores workday settings; the existing pace engine remains the personalized projection.

`likelyStranded` is a conservative capacity conclusion, while `theoreticallyReachable` only says enough short-window capacity can become available under full use. A range-based verdict appears after at least two qualifying candidates; a lone candidate must include at least three percentage points of long-window movement before it can be displayed.

## Scope

This is a spec-only draft for design review. It does not change runtime behavior and does not close the feature issue.

Refs #2261 and the maintainer direction in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2261#issuecomment-5006555635

## Validation

- fresh product-reader review: pass
- fresh repository-architecture review: pass
- post-review lifecycle reader: pass
- post-review math/presentation reader: pass
- staged diff and whitespace checks: pass
- Swift tests not run (documentation-only change)

target.title: Add DI composition root and navigation/activation seam for tray view models
target.body:
## Summary

Introduces the dependency-injection and navigation plumbing that page view models will depend on: a root `ServiceProvider` owned by `App`, a navigation scope/activation seam, and a UI-thread dispatcher abstraction. This is **additive infrastructure only** — no page is converted to MVVM and no existing `App` behavior is moved. **Intended runtime behavior change: none.**

## What this adds

- **DI composition root.** Adds `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` (10.0.0). `App` builds one root `ServiceProvider` with `ValidateScopes` + `ValidateOnBuild`, **after** tray initialization, and disposes it via an ordered shutdown step. App-owned services (`SettingsManager`, `IAppCommands`) are registered as **pre-built instances**, so the container never disposes them — `App` keeps sole ownership and there is **no double-dispose**. A build/validation failure is logged and leaves the provider null, so this plumbing can never prevent the tray from starting.
- **`Presentation/` WinUI-free core:** `IUiDispatcher`, `INavigationAware`, `INavigationService`, `IPageActivator`, `NavigationScopeManager` (owns the per-navigation DI scope and the view-model activate/deactivate/dispose lifetime; navigation is non-re-entrant and exception-safe), `AppNavigationService`, and transient `SettingsPageViewModel`/`PermissionsPageViewModel` placeholders. Hand-linked into the pure `net10` test project.
- **`Presentation/Adapters/` WinUI-bound:** `WinUIDispatcher`, `FramePageActivator`.
- **Navigation activation hook** in `HubWindow.OnContentFrameNavigated`. The page→view-model map is empty, so it is a **runtime no-op today**: it only advances the navigation scope and never touches a page's `DataContext`, navigation, back-stack, rail selection, or dedupe. HubWindow's existing navigation is untouched.

## Ownership / ledger

Adds three `authoritative` rows with behavioral guard tests — `ui-dispatcher` (`IUiDispatcher`), `navigation-scope` (`NavigationScopeManager`), `composition-root` (`AppServiceRegistration`) — plus matching single-source-owner entries.

## Validation

- `build.ps1`: pass (all projects)
- `dotnet test OpenClaw.Shared.Tests`: 2865 passed / 31 skipped (incl. architecture-ledger consistency)
- `dotnet test OpenClaw.Tray.Tests`: 1772 passed (incl. 30 presentation unit + source-contract tests covering: no double-dispose of App-owned instances, transient view-model disposal with scope, non-re-entrant navigation, `Activate`/`Deactivate`-throws scope disposal, `Reset()` window-close teardown + re-navigation, A→B deactivate/dispose-before-activate ordering, `ValidateOnBuild`, the WinUI-free boundary, and the ordered shutdown-disposal step)

## Real behavior proof

Verified against a local Debug build of this branch (node reports `0.6.13-bkudiess-pr4-di-navigation-seam.1`), non-isolated tray, real gateway node.

- **Tray launch — DI root builds at runtime:** log emits `Service provider initialized.` on launch (observed across 3 launches). This is the `InitializeServiceProvider()` success line, proving `BuildServiceProvider(ValidateScopes + ValidateOnBuild)` succeeds in a real tray process after tray init, with no validation throw.
- **Node / MCP healthy on this build:** gateway handshake `caps=6, commands=25`; `winnode --list-tools` returns 52 tools; node connected in `node` mode.
- **Representative navigation:** multiple deep-link navigations handled and `ConnectionPage` rendered; `OnContentFrameNavigated` runs the new activation hook each time with no errors — confirming the hook is a safe no-op today.
- **Hub close / reopen (isolated current-head build, HEAD `4ed87980`):** on an isolated temp profile (`EnableMcpServer=true`; real `%APPDATA%` untouched):
  - Provider init across 2 launches: `[INFO] Service provider initialized.`; startup logs `[MCP] HTTP server listening on http://<host>:8765/`, `Started MCP-only node service without gateway connection`, `Application started (WinUI 3)`.
  - Hub **opened** via `winnode --command app.navigate {"page":"permissions"}` → `navigated:true` (Companion window present in `list_apps`).
  - Hub **closed** via a computer-use click on the title-bar Close button → window removed from `list_apps`, i.e. `HubWindow.Closed` fired and the `IPageActivator.Reset()` path ran, with **no exception logged**.
  - Hub **reopened** via `app.navigate {"page":"connection"}` → `navigated:true` (fresh navigation after `Reset()`), **no exception** (only a benign, unrelated `[WARN] [ConnectionPage] Could not subscribe to High Contrast changes`).
  - Full-log error scan: the only `[ERROR]` is `Previous session did not exit cleanly` (from an earlier `Stop-Process` kill of a prior probe instance, not PR code) — no `ObjectDisposedException`, no `failed disposing`, no lifecycle exceptions.
- **Clean shutdown — live-proven:** this PR adds `SafeShutdownStepAsync("service provider", …)` which nulls `_services` and then awaits `ServiceProvider.DisposeAsync()`. Captured live at current head (`4ed87980`) by clicking the tray Close on the isolated build:
  ```
  [2026-07-17 11:54:40.817] [INFO] Shutdown: disposing service provider
  [2026-07-17 11:54:40.820] [INFO] Shutdown: disposed service provider
  ```
  The full ordered sequence confirms the intended lifecycle: windows/services torn down first (OpenTelemetry endpoint, node service, ssh tunnel, pairing approval, chat window, setup window, tray menu window, keep-alive window) → **then** `service provider` → **then** tray icon → single-instance mutex → deep link token source → `Shutdown complete; calling Exit() now`. `disposed service provider` appears exactly **once** (no double-dispose), there is **no** `Shutdown: failed disposing` line and **no** `ObjectDisposedException`, and the `_services = null` before `await DisposeAsync()` fix ran cleanly (no late `Frame.Navigated` fault). Corroborated by `PresentationSeamContractTests.App_DisposesServiceProvider_DuringShutdown`, `App_NullsServiceProviderField_BeforeAwaitingDisposal`, and `AppServiceRegistrationTests.Dispose_DoesNotDisposeAppOwnedInstanceSingletons`.

## Follow-ups

- When pages gain view models, wrap the `OnContentFrameNavigated` activation-hook body in try/catch-and-log so a misbehaving view model `Activate`/`Deactivate` cannot surface as an unhandled exception in the frame-navigated handler.
- Reintroduce a shutdown-safe awaitable UI-marshaling method on `IUiDispatcher` if/when a consumer needs it.
